answers.answer: Starting hands are 4 cards each for 2 players, 3 each for 3 players, and 2 each for 4 players. Remove the Epidemic cards and set them aside before dealing; shuffle and deal the remaining City and Event cards. Each player's matching pawn starts in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 5–6: matching pawns in Atlanta; Epidemics set aside; starting-card table.

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2 space. Reveal 3 Infection cards and place 3 matching cubes in each named city; reveal 3 more and place 2 in each; reveal 3 more and place 1 in each. Put all 9 revealed cards on the Infection Discard Pile; the remaining cards form the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 8: marker on leftmost 2; 3/2/1 cube groups; nine cards to discard pile, rest form deck.

answers.answer: Use 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic, removing unused Epidemic cards from the game. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles, as equal in size as possible; shuffle one Epidemic into each pile and stack them with smaller piles on the bottom.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: difficulty counts, unused cards removed, equal-as-possible piles, one Epidemic per pile, smaller piles on bottom.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions; you may repeat actions or stop early. Discarded action-cost cards go to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together, resolve Epidemics first and reduce/play Events to the 7-card limit; next infect cities. After all three phases, play passes to the left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Actions: up to 4 actions, repetitions/stopping allowed, Player Discard Pile; then draw, infect, and pass left.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry moves along a white line to a connected city at no card cost. Direct Flight discards the City card for the destination. Charter Flight discards the City card matching your current city to move anywhere. Shuttle Flight requires being at a research station and moves to another research station at no card cost. White lines that go off one board edge wrap to the other edge (the summary gives Sydney and Los Angeles as an example).
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table and Special Rules & Edge Cases: board wrapping.

answers.answer: Normally, discard the City card matching your current city, take a research station from the supply, and place it there. If all 6 are already built, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If the box supplied more than 6, set extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Other Actions, Build a Research Station; Special Rules & Edge Cases: station limit and extras.

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action removes 1 cube of one chosen color from that city; because the two other colors are cured, an action for either of those colors removes all cubes of that color from the city. Each different color requires a separate action. Removed cubes return to the cube supply.
answers.evidence: Other Actions, Treat Disease: 1 cube, or all cubes of one cured color; separate actions by color; cubes returned to supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of the same disease color (4 for the Scientist) and move that disease's cure marker to its Cure Indicator. The station city's color need not match. Existing cubes remain, and the disease can still infect during infections and Epidemics until eradicated. If no cubes of that color are on the board when cured, it is immediately eradicated and its marker is flipped.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure: station, card cost, marker movement, existing cubes/infections; immediate eradication if no cubes.

answers.answer: Normally, the only card that can be transferred is the City card matching the city both players occupy. The players must agree. If the recipient goes over 7 cards, they must immediately discard or play an Event card until within the limit.
answers.evidence: Other Actions, Share Knowledge; Hand Limit: applies immediately after receiving cards, including through Share Knowledge.

answers.answer: The Researcher may give any City card from the Researcher's hand to a player in the same city, on either player's turn. The exception does not let another player give the Researcher an arbitrary nonmatching City card; that transfer must still match the city. Both players must agree under the normal Share Knowledge rule.
answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases, Researcher exception: any card from Researcher's hand, either player's turn, and no arbitrary nonmatching card to Researcher.

answers.answer: After actions, draw 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 remain when you need to draw, the game ends and players lose. Discards are not reshuffled.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: draw top 2 together; fewer than 2 means loss; do not reshuffle discards.

answers.answer: Resolve the Epidemic in order: Increase the Infection Rate marker by one space; Infect by drawing the bottom Infection card and placing 3 matching-color cubes unless that disease is eradicated. Because the city has 2 cubes, add only enough to reach 3, then an outbreak occurs. Discard that Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile. Intensify by reshuffling only the Infection Discard Pile and placing it on top of the Infection Deck. Remove the resolved Epidemic from the game; do not draw a replacement.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards, steps 1–3: Increase, bottom-card Infect with add-to-3/outbreak rule, discard, Intensify; no replacement.

answers.answer: After 0 through 6 Epidemics, respectively, flip 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, and 4 Infection cards per turn.
answers.evidence: Player Reference, Infection Rate Track table: Epidemics Resolved 0–6 maps to 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4 cards.

answers.answer: Resolve the first Epidemic through all three steps, then resolve the second through all three steps; Events may be played between them. Reduce an over-limit hand only after resolving all Epidemic cards drawn, by discarding or playing Events until within 7.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: both are resolved fully in sequence and Events may be played between; Drawing Player Cards/Hand Limit: resolve all Epidemics before enforcing the limit.

answers.answer: Flip Infection cards from the top of the Infection Deck, one at a time, in a quantity equal to the current infection rate. For a normal disease, place 1 matching cube in the named city; if that city already has 3 of that color, do not add a fourth and trigger an outbreak. For an eradicated disease, place no cube. A cured but not eradicated disease can still receive cubes. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities: top of deck, infection-rate count, one at a time, placement/outbreak, eradication; Cure Procedure says cured disease can still infect.

answers.answer: When an outbreak occurs, advance the Outbreaks marker by 1 and place 1 cube of that color in every connected city. A connected city already holding 3 cubes triggers a chain-reaction outbreak after the current outbreak resolves. Do not add cubes to a city that has already had an outbreak while resolving the current Infection card, so spread does not add another cube back into the first city. The three-cube cap is per color; a city can hold multiple colors, up to 3 cubes of each.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks: marker movement, spread, chain timing, no cubes added to cities already erupted during that card; city cap is per color.

answers.answer: No. Once the Infection card has been drawn, Airlift cannot be played between drawing it and resolving it. After that card resolves, Airlift may be played before the next Infection card, at any time outside the draw-to-resolution interval. Any player may play it; the player playing it chooses its use. It costs no action, and the played Event goes to the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Events may be played at any time but not between drawing and resolving a card; player chooses use and discards to Player Discard Pile. Airlift effect moves a pawn.

answers.answer: As an action, the Contingency Planner takes 1 Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and stores it on the Role card. The storage limit is 1 and it does not count against the hand limit. When played, remove it from the game rather than discarding it.
answers.evidence: Roles, Contingency Planner: action, anywhere in discard pile, limit 1, excluded from hand limit, removed from game on play.

answers.answer: As an action, the Dispatcher may move any pawn to a city with another pawn, or move another player's pawn as if it were their own. Moving another player's pawn requires the owner's agreement. For Direct/Charter Flights while directing another pawn, the cards come from the Dispatcher's hand; a Charter card matches the moved pawn's departure city. The Dispatcher cannot direct another pawn to Treat Disease or perform other nonmovement actions, and cannot use the Operations Expert's special move.
answers.evidence: Roles, Dispatcher: both movement options, owner agreement, card payer and Charter departure city, no nonmovement actions, no Operations Expert special move.

answers.answer: Players win immediately when cures for all 4 diseases are discovered; diseases need not be eradicated and cubes may remain. The three loss triggers are: the Outbreaks marker reaches the last space (8th outbreak); the needed color's cube supply is exhausted and required cubes cannot be placed, including during an Epidemic, outbreak, or infection; or a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after their actions.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: immediate win upon all cures and three defeats; Cube supply check specifies immediate loss if needed cubes cannot be placed.
